Tonight's plan

Astronomical dark divided into 10-minute slots, every eligible target scored in every slot, the winners coalesced into blocks of at least 45 minutes, at most 3 targets — a switch costs a slew, a plate solve and an autofocus, so churn is a real cost. Only projects with at least 1 h on record are scheduled: below that the fractional formula always prefers whatever has least data (a 0.88 h toehold took the whole night in testing), so the toehold tier is ranked separately, exactly as it is in the table below. Frame counts are the REALISTIC figure: the MEASURED 61 s median cadence (four nights, 679 subs) at 82% duty for dither, autofocus and plate solves — 74 s per frame — less 18 min for any meridian flip inside a block. Existing hours are discounted by how well they merge with tonight's settings, and count only if they were shot from Haxtun — another sky is never stacked with this one and counts as 0 h. Tonight's settings are gain 0 / 60 s, read from the 400 most recent frames on the drive. Full credit at the same gain and exposure; 93% at another gain (an estimate from one NGC 7331 experiment, good to a few percent at best); 93% at another exposure (NOT measured on Haxtun data — borrowed from the gain figure). Focal length is not a cohort key at all — measured 2026-10-02, Siril solves a 3% scale change from the stars alone.

Fractional improvement

sqrt((h + added) / h) per 10-minute slot, where h is the EFFECTIVE depth already on disk. Favours thin data. ⚠ Not the same ordering as the table or the ★ pick: those weigh the whole night a target is up, this weighs each slot alone, so the thinnest project that is up takes every slot it can — the ★ pick may not appear here at all.

Deepen — targets you already have

Hours are split by the camera angle MEASURED from the filenames and weighted by EXPOSURE TIME (folded mod 180, so a 180° pair is one framing). Payoff is the SNR gain from what tonight can realistically add at 82% duty; the "deep enough" gate is a depth policy judged on a further full night, not on tonight. Moon separation is measured only while the target and the moon share the sky. Payoff is computed on EFFECTIVE depth, not on the "on disk" column: hours shot from another sky count 0, and hours at a different GAIN or EXPOSURE count at 93% (estimates — see the plan notes). Where the two differ, the line beneath the payoff says how many effective hours it was computed on. Mixed-exposure piles want stacking per exposure, merged by inverse variance.
